question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 depletion after washout
ideas.description: Use an auxin-inducible degron (e.g., AID2) to remove FOS or JUN after the stimulus is withdrawn and measure whether target gene expression and chromatin states persist. If memory collapses on depletion, AP-1 is required to maintain it rather than just to write it.

ideas.title: Enhancer motif mutants tested for chromatin memory
ideas.description: CRISPR-mutate AP-1 motifs in candidate memory enhancers, then run ATAC-seq and H3K27ac time courses after washout in wild-type and mutant cells. Loss of persistence at mutant enhancers would show that AP-1 binding is required for chromatin-level memory.

ideas.title: Pulsed optogenetic training with hysteresis readout
ideas.description: Drive AP-1 with light pulses that vary in frequency, number, and spacing, then measure gene expression and the speed and magnitude of re-induction after a rest period. This tests whether the system encodes stimulus history and how the encoding depends on pulse pattern.

ideas.title: Barcoded lineage tracing of memory across divisions
ideas.description: Pair AP-1-responsive reporters with heritable barcodes and track single-cell memory states across many generations. Tracking whether the primed state is passed to daughters, and at what fidelity, distinguishes heritable memory from memory that is re-established each cycle.

ideas.title: Synthetic AP-1 feedback circuit for bistability
ideas.description: Build an AP-1 autoregulatory loop in a controlled cell line and test whether it sustains expression after the inducer is removed, and whether it shows bistable switching. This checks whether AP-1 self-reinforcement is sufficient for memory, independent of native chromatin context.

candidates: Degron-tag FOS/JUN (e.g., AID2) and deplete after stimulus washout to test whether AP-1 is required to maintain the memory
Time-course CUT&RUN/ChIP-seq of AP-1 occupancy after stimulus washout to see whether binding outlasts the signal
Barcoded single-cell lineage tracing with AP-1-responsive reporters to test whether memory is inherited across divisions
Optogenetic or pulsed AP-1 induction at varied frequency and duration to measure hysteresis and dose/frequency encoding
Re-stimulation kinetics: compare magnitude and speed of target gene induction on a second exposure (priming)
ATAC-seq time course at AP-1 enhancers after washout to test whether chromatin opening persists
Histone mark persistence (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) at primed enhancers over days to weeks after stimulus removal
CRISPR mutation of AP-1 motifs in candidate memory enhancers, then test whether chromatin and transcriptional memory are lost
Synthetic AP-1 autoregulatory feedback circuit to test whether it can produce bistability and self-sustained expression
Fluorescent dilution assays to measure how memory is partitioned between daughter cells over generations
Mitotic chromatin profiling to test whether AP-1 bookmarks target loci through cell division
Live imaging of FOS transcriptional bursting reporters to see whether burst frequency encodes a stored state
Phosphoproteomics of JUN/FOS and co-factors to determine whether post-translational marks persist after stimulus removal
Measure FOS and JUN protein half-lives and test whether they match the observed memory duration
Knock out chromatin writers and erasers (p300/CBP, KDM family) to see whether memory depends on epigenetic maintenance
Adoptive transfer or in vivo stimulus exposure to test AP-1 memory in primary T cells or macrophages
Multi-tissue in vivo profiling after a chronic stimulus (stress, injury, diet) to map persistent AP-1 signatures
Heterodimer composition shifts (FOS/JUN vs ATF3 or JDP2) tracked as a readout of stimulus history
Cell-to-cell variability and clonal analysis to distinguish deterministic from stochastic memory
Mathematical models fit to perturbation data to compare memory mechanisms (bistability, epigenetic, protein stability)
